trial_court: Senior Civil Judge at Yadgir in RA No. 18/2010
case_name: Basalingamma D/O Mallayya Ors vs Mallayya S/O Basanna Ors

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Basalingamma D/O Mallayya, Ishamma D/O Mallayya, Indramma W/O Mallayya (minor's mother), all minors under the age of 18 years
parties.respondent_defendant: Mallayya S/O Basanna, Basanana S/O Bhimaya @ Mallappa, Bassamma W/O. Bassanana, Maremma W/O. Maribasappa Konkatdar, Basalingappa S/O Basanana (all respondents)

facts_of_case: The petitioners are minors under the age of 18 years seeking partition of property. The trial court decreed the suit for partition in favour of plaintiff Nos.1 and 2 and dismissed the suit in its entirety.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party seeking partition to prove that the properties are ancestral joint family properties.
legal_principles.held: It is asserted that the suit properties are the ancestral joint family properties and they are in joint possession.

legal_principles.principle: The court will grant partition and separate possession to the parties seeking it if they prove that the properties are ancestral joint family properties.
legal_principles.held: The plaintiffs assert that defendant No.1 has neglected the plaintiffs and driven them out of the house by ill-treating and attempted to alienate the suit properties. Hence, they filed a suit for partition and separate possession.

outcome.final_order: The judgment and decree passed by the first appellate Court are set aside, and the judgment and decree passed by the Trial Court are restored.

use_for_drafting: advising on Hindu Marriage Act implications
